description: Make backend startup resilient to config validation failures. Currently, validate_production_secrets in apps/backend/app/config.py raises ValueError for conditions like ADMIN_JWT_SECRET == JWT_PRIVATE_KEY or missing EDGE_SHARED_SECRET. This crashes Settings() instantiation at module level (line ~243: settings = Settings()), which prevents main.py from importing config, which prevents the FastAPI lifespan from ever running init_mongo() and init_redis(). The fix must ensure the app STARTS (so health checks return useful diagnostics) rather than crash silently.
steps: In apps/backend/app/config.py, modify the validate_production_secrets model_validator (mode='after') to convert all ValueError raises into logger.error() calls instead. The validator should never prevent the app from starting. Specifically: (1) The EDGE_SHARED_SECRET check in production should log error instead of raising. (2) The JWT_SECRET placeholder check should log error instead of raising. (3) The JWT_SECRET length check should log error instead of raising. (4) The ADMIN_JWT_SECRET required check should log error instead of raising. (5) The ADMIN_JWT_SECRET == JWT_PRIVATE_KEY check should log error instead of raising. (6) The RS256 JWT_PRIVATE_KEY/JWT_PUBLIC_KEY checks should log error instead of raising. Always return self at the end.

Add a new property or field to the Settings class called `startup_errors: list[str]` that collects all the validation errors that would have been raised. Initialize it as an empty list. In validate_production_secrets, instead of raising, append the error message to self.startup_errors and log it. This allows the health endpoint to report what went wrong.

In apps/backend/app/api/v1/health.py, update the basic_health_check endpoint to include startup_errors from settings if any exist. Import settings and check if settings.startup_errors is non-empty. If so, return status 'degraded' with a 'config_errors' field listing the issues. This gives operators visibility into why services are not initializing properly.

Add a test in apps/backend/tests/test_config_resilience.py that verifies Settings() can be instantiated with APP_ENV='production' and invalid/missing secrets without raising an exception. Test that startup_errors is populated correctly.
acceptance_criteria: Settings() instantiation with APP_ENV='production' and ADMIN_JWT_SECRET == JWT_PRIVATE_KEY does NOT raise ValueError
Settings() instantiation with APP_ENV='production' and missing EDGE_SHARED_SECRET does NOT raise ValueError
Settings().startup_errors contains descriptive error messages for each validation failure
The /health endpoint returns 'degraded' status with config_errors when startup_errors exist
Running pytest tests/ passes with no failures
verification: cd apps/backend && python -c "import os; os.environ['APP_ENV']='production'; os.environ['JWT_SECRET']='short'; from app.config import Settings; s = Settings(); print('startup_errors:', s.startup_errors); assert len(s.startup_errors) > 0; print('PASS: Settings did not crash')"
findings: All 227 existing tests pass. Required pytest-env plugin for pytest.ini env setting to work. The project requires Python 3.10+ (uses str | None syntax). pyenv local 3.11.15 was used. The requirements.txt has strict pinning that prevented direct pip install -r requirements.txt (aiohappyeyeballs==2.6.2 not available on system Python 3.9 but is on 3.11). Installed deps individually with relaxed versions instead.
